answer: In PoA, each bonded identity is an escrowed claim, so coordinated equivocation by k identities incurs a quadratic penalty, O(k^2), reflecting pairwise conflict evidence rather than a linear per-node fee. Upon detection, an exponential capital-loss multiplier applies to the sybil controller, asymmetrically eroding collateral and making large swarms uneconomic: a relic in the nebula cannot reach the zenith by splitting its name.
